what: The header of the gate catalogue: the version a project freezes. Declared BY HAND. Any change to a key covered by the content hash raises the version and is recorded in the changelog with the hash it produced; regenerating the published file without touching a covered key leaves it alone.

method.name: Urazuke
method.license_note: Apache-2.0 is the licence of what a machine runs or consumes mechanically: the programs of build/, their tests in tests/, this gate definition in gates/ and its published copies (docs/html/api/gates.json and docs/html/api/index.json). The prose of the method -- its documents, its contracts, its manuals, its eight translations, its prompts and the labels extracted from it -- is CC BY-SA 4.0. The split, with the reason for each side, is in LICENCIA.md; the two legal texts are LICENSE-CODE and LICENSE. A rule statement travels on both sides on purpose: the same holder can license his own text twice, and what he cannot do is leave the consumer guessing which one governs.

changelog.changed: First published version. The base is identical to what the tool had compiled (gates/baseline.json). Coming in, declared with since_schema 2: the forty-five rules of Annex H with their switches, severities, instruments and scoreboard (D-043 to D-049); the five anchors at steps 5, 8, 9, 10 and 12 with their four new evaluators; the inheritance of the five anchors by the legacy path when it enters the loop at step 5; and the D-042 additions to steps 13, 15 and 23, plus the mandatory mutation testing of step 9. The data layer is published in English (D-051).

No requirement changed. The language declaration now tells the truth: the published file is bilingual, because the frozen base keeps the Spanish it was frozen in (the exception declared in D-051) while everything new is in English. `languages.data` said `en`, so a consumer that trusted it would show Spanish to an English reader. It now says `mixed` and carries `text_language`, a mechanical rule that says which language each text is in, plus the instruction a consumer needs: read the opaque `id` and take the text from your own catalogue. Raising the version is not decoration: a key covered by the hash changed, so the content of 2026.10.1 and the content of this version are different, and a project that froze one has to be able to tell them apart.

No requirement changed: the data layer stops naming tools. The published file carried five references to the tool that had this definition compiled before the method took ownership of it (D-050): two inside the frozen base -- the sizing verification of step 3, which named that tool and its gate id, and the label of the cyclic report artifact of step 22, which named one of its commands -- one in the description of the sizing evaluator, which cited that gate id again, and two in the language declaration, which named the frozen base by a file name that carried the tool name. The method owns this definition and publishes it for any consumer, so a tool named in the data reads as a dependency, and there is none. The owner authorised editing the two frozen texts as an explicit exception to base_is_frozen, written down in D-055: nothing else of the base moved, and the provenance of the freeze stays inside gates/baseline.json, which is not published. The frozen base was renamed from its previous file name to gates/baseline.json so that not even the path names a tool. A test now turns red if a tool or protocol name enters the published level again.

Two changes, both from the step 23 retrospective on the first adaptation of the method to another format. One requirement comes in and one note stops being false. The new requirement is at step 20: the run of the recovery manual by a person who does not program now has to leave its record -- the measured end-to-end time, the exact point where the person got stuck and every word they did not understand, with a date and a name -- and every one of those words opens a pending item. The gate already demanded the run; what it did not demand was its evidence, so a run that produced nothing counted as fulfilled, which is the same defect as a green step that measured nothing. It comes in as a NEW verify entry with its since_schema, and it is checked by a person reading the record, which is why it declares no artifact path: the method does not name a file for it and a name invented here would be published as a default. The note that stops being false belongs to the two prior inputs of Annex H (the user glossary and the list of profiles): it said the step 2 contract did not ask for them yet, and since 2026-10-26 it does, in writing and named from the project file, with its own completeness check. The path stays undeclared on purpose, for the same reason: the owner never declared one.

One requirement comes in and one note stops being true, and both are the same decision: the two prior inputs of Annex H -- the user glossary and the list of profiles -- now have a canonical path declared by the owner, docs/GLOSSARY.md and docs/PROFILES.md. Until today the method asked for them in the step 2 contract and declared no path, so the catalogue published them as required and not measurable by machine: a gate cannot look at a file whose name nobody knows, and the matrix of step 5 could keep being invented against a list that nothing obliged to exist. They come in as NEW step 2 artifacts with their since_schema, with min_bytes and no must_contain, because what those two files have to SAY is judged by a person and a pattern invented here would publish a default the owner never declared. The frozen base is untouched. Note for a consumer that froze 2026.10.4: the two prior inputs change from declared: false / path: null to declared: true with their path, so a tool that branched on declared has a new branch to take.

Two findings of the external audit close together, because both move the fingerprint and a version is one content and one only. First: `counts` and `what` were the only two keys of the published file that could change without breaking verification, and they are now COVERED. A summary of quantities that can lie is worse than no summary -- a tool that uses it to check it finished reading would accept a truncated file in silence -- and `what` is where the file states the scope of its own protection. Nothing else about them changed: same values, same meaning. Second: the languages of the prose are now declared as a LIST, `languages.prose_versions`, instead of as a count inside a sentence. The claim lived in this note, in the prompt corpus, in two README files and in forty strings of a landing page, so correcting one sentence meant mechanically raising two declared versions; from here on, adding a language changes an array and no prose. And the method declares ITS OWN languages: the list was inherited from another specification's, which already moved on, so the sentence had gone stale on its own. No requirement, no id and no threshold changed in this version.

The method writes down what a project pins and what it costs to change it, and it says so in the data because a consumer is the one who pins. Three things come in and no requirement, no id and no threshold changes. First, a new covered key, `pinning`: a project pins ONE catalog_version with the content hash that version declares, and raising it mid-project is a REGRESSION of the completeness state -- a version that adds a requirement to a step already closed reopens that step, and an installation that cannot measure a newly required evaluator reports declared and not measured, so the step does not advance. That is the mechanism by which an upgrade stops a project, and it is intended. Raising the version is the owner decision, written with its date; raising it in silence is not allowed. Second, the obligation on the consumer, declared instead of left to be guessed: a tool that pins RECORDS the pair (catalog_version, content_hash) by those names and CONTRASTS it against the version ledger, which lives in the method repository and not on the host that served the file; on a mismatch it says which of the two moved and it is red, never a silent re-pin to whatever the host serves today. And what is forbidden: pinning to an internal compiled identity that the method cannot name -- it looks like pinning and it is not, because nobody outside the tool can audit it and the differential cannot be computed. This was measured on 2026-10-27: a consumer that already pinned, and pinned correctly in its own terms, pinned to an identity that is not a catalog_version and appears in no ledger. The data said what to freeze and never said what to freeze it BY. Third, the differential becomes computable: every entry the method added after the freeze now declares `since_version`, the published version in which it first appeared, because `since_schema` only separates the frozen base from everything added later and that is too coarse to count what enters between two published versions. Thirty-five entries, with their provenance measured against the history of the sources: thirty-two arrived with 2026.10.1, one with 2026.10.4 and two with 2026.10.5. A base entry declares no provenance, because the base is in every published version, and the validator rejects both omissions and a provenance pointing at a version nobody published. One correction inside this same version, before it was published: the clause that tells the consumer what to contrast against pointed at a key of the sources that no published payload carries, and the index of this interface declared only the human page of the ledger, so the one consumer that implemented the obligation had to guess the address it downloads. Both are fixed here and the recorded hash is the corrected content. The hash of a version is never edited once that version is served; this one never was -- the canonical host was serving 2026.10.6 while this entry lived in an unmerged branch -- and bumping instead would have recorded a version that nobody can ever fetch, which is a worse lie than this note (PND-056).

The method says how one asks. Until 2026-10-27 the prompts ordered the model to ASK twenty-two times, in fifteen of the twenty-seven files of the published corpus, and nothing anywhere said HOW: the form was left to improvisation and the owner got the question loose, without the data that justifies it, without options and without a recommendation. It is the same asymmetry step 11 pursues, in the direction that costs the most, and the same family as two things the method already did: step 8 did not settle for show me the red and defined what a receipt is, step 12 did not settle for report and separated verified from believed. Two things come in and no id, no threshold and no existing requirement changes. First, a new rule: UX-28, family B6 -- a sixth usability family, the first one that is not about the screen the system shows a person but about the conversation in which the system gets built. It demands four parts in order (the data that makes the question necessary, listed; one paragraph of no more than five lines that links that data and lets the question be seen; the question with its possible answers numbered; the agent recommendation) and the technical depth the project declared. It WARNS, it does not block, and it is a human red verified at pending close, for the reason the annex already declares for CQ-12 and CQ-14: a gate can verify the clause is in the seventy-two prompts and in the eight languages, and no test can verify that a concrete question written on a Tuesday has its four parts. It does not enter the compliance percentage; it is reported as human verification coverage. Second, the parameter: project_config.communication_depth, one of beginner, decision_maker or technical, undeclared meaning decision_maker with the agent saying which one it used. The name and the three values are declared here so no consuming tool has to guess them. And one thing worth saying because it looks like a contradiction: this rule goes INSIDE the prompts, which is what D-044 argued against. It is the written exception and it is narrow -- the clause names the four parts and the parameter and nothing else, the full statement still lives once in the annex -- and the reason is that the other forty-five are demands on the system being built, measured over artifacts, while this one is a demand on the conversation, and the only way for the model to obey it is for it to be in what the model reads. The exception does not authorize copying any of the others. And one thing this version fixes inside itself, because UX-28 was the first rule the method added after the pinning machinery of D-068 existed: a rule can now declare since_schema and since_version like any other entry, and the upgrade differential counts it. Without that the differential would have omitted a new rule in silence, which is the kind of summary that can lie that D-067 already closed for the counts. The hash recorded here is the corrected content; this version was never served (D-070, PND-054).

A pointer that this file publishes now resolves for a consumer that only has this file, and the defect was one day old. 2026.10.8 published the UX-28 parameter as project_config.communication_depth and described it as "One of communication_depth" -- and no key of the published payload carried that name: the three values lived only in the sources, which are not published. Measured over the served file: beginner appeared zero times, decision_maker and technical only inside English prose. So a tool that wanted to validate the depth a project declared had to GUESS the list and could see two of the three values mentioned, which is a partial list that reads as complete and is worse than none. It is the same family D-069 closed the day before -- a key path a published text names has to resolve in the published file -- committed one day later, in the first new entry since the rule was written, and the pointer guard did not see it for a reason that can be named: it only recognises paths with a DOT, and "One of communication_depth" is a bare token. It said zero findings and that was true for the pointers it knew how to see. What comes in: project_config now publishes `enums`, the value list of every field that names one, DERIVED from the single copy in the sources so there are never two lists that can diverge, plus `enums_what` saying what the block is and why it exists; the field names it as `project_config.enums.communication_depth` and lists the three values in prose, so the path resolves under rule A as well; the validator refuses a field that names an enum by a bare name or one that does not exist (E_ENUM_CONFIGURACION); and the pointer guard gains rule E, which is rule A for the shape rule A could not see, symmetric in both directions -- a published enum that no field names is also a finding, because it is a copy with no consumer. No requirement, no id, no threshold and no rule changed in this version: the only new content is the resolved list of three values that were already published in prose. One honesty note, written because it is what makes the guard falsifiable: this one WOULD have caught the defect that originated it -- measured against the published tree of deb06ce it names the bare token, and against today it finds none (D-071, PND-059).

Two things that were declared and incomplete, closed together because both live in what this file says about itself. First: every declared version now has an address of its own. The canonical URL serves whatever is current, so a tool that pointed at it was updated in silence and the hash moved under its feet -- and since the pinning contract of 2026.10.7 that stopped being a nicety: the data told a project to pin a version and keep it to the end, and there was no address from which to read the pinned version back. This file said so itself, in prior_version_content: "There is no per-version URL on this host today". Now there is one per resource folder and per version, with no purge, and the index declares the base, the current address and the full list of versions that have one, so no consumer derives an address. What the address promises is the content whose hash the ledger records for that version, not the bytes: the excluded keys are publication metadata and a regeneration moves them. Recovered and verified for every version already published: 14 copies, 9 of this catalogue and 5 of the prompt corpus, each one recomputing to the hash its own ledger entry records. Second: `what` now carries, in one single copy shared with the prompt corpus and with the index, the SCOPE of what the hash protects -- self-consistent, detects truncation, a bad merge and hand editing, does not protect against an adversary who controls the host, and there is no cryptographic signature, which is a written decision and not an oversight. That sentence had been in the index since 2026.10.2 and the index carries no hash of its own by design, so it travelled unprotected: a security declaration in an unprotected field is one an attacker can edit to say the opposite. It could only move here once `what` was covered, which happened in 2026.10.6. No requirement, no id, no threshold and no rule changed (D-073, PND-008, PND-009).

The escalation of CQ-18 gains the threshold id it was already being declared through, and the absence of a declaration stops meaning two things at once. CQ-18 (basic accessibility) warns from day one and escalates to blocks when the product has end users outside the organisation (D-048). The rule said the escalation requires a declaration by the owner through the same mechanism as any threshold, and that mechanism is by threshold id: the project declares thresholds by id and whatever is not declared is reported as undeclared, never invented. There was no id for this one. Measured on 2026-10-29: the five published threshold ids are lines_per_file, lines_per_function, paths_per_function, minimum_coverage and mutation_target, and none of them is this condition, so an owner who decided well that the product has no users outside the organisation had nowhere to write it. What that cost is not the decision, it is the audit six months later: the absence of a key read the same for an escalation DECLINED with a reason and for an escalation nobody ever looked at, which is the defect D-057 already named in another scale -- a state that cannot be told from not having been measured. And the trap next door, measured because it is the obvious shortcut: project_config.real_users means something else. A tool for internal staff can have two hundred real users and zero users outside the organisation, so reusing that field would escalate the rule to blocking in silence in exactly the project the escalation does not apply to. What comes in: one entry in adapters.thresholds, end_users_outside_the_organisation, with value null and declared false like any threshold the method does not fix, declared_by the owner, and its provenance (since_schema 2, since_version 2026.10.11); the clause of escalates_to.requires now names it and states the three states -- true blocks, false records the escalation as declined, no declaration is an undeclared threshold and the escalation is pending; and the validator now walks the thresholds for provenance, so the next threshold cannot come in without saying which version it entered. The id is a boolean and not a number because what a threshold declares is a value, and the value here is whether the condition holds. Its spelling follows the words the rule already uses -- outside the organisation -- because ids are append-only and are never renamed. No requirement changed, no id was recycled, no severity moved: CQ-18 still warns, and it still escalates under exactly the condition D-048 wrote. What this version does NOT do, said by its name: force any project to declare it. A project that declares nothing reads as an undeclared threshold, which is the state that was missing (D-076, PND-062).

Two rules enter and, with them, a shape this catalogue did not have: a rule with FACES. Where the two came from, because that is what makes them rules and not advice: eleven failures measured on 2026-11-01 inside an experiment that was measuring something else, all of them with the same shape -- an instrument that could not look and reported it exactly as it reports health, or that looked at less than it believed it had looked at -- and reached through eleven different paths, which is what makes it implausible that this is the defect of one program. The measured ones, in one line each: a guard that read a figure as zero and could not tell the zero that means there is nothing from the zero that means it could not look, while the real desynchronisation it was meant to catch was 28 of 47; an instrument that depended on the very resource it measures, so the resource falling over reported health; a filter whose option stopped being an option after a bare double dash and returned 816 where the answer was 2, which is the same demand with the sign inverted -- I found nothing because I did not run, against I found everything because I did not filter --; a local check more permissive than the one that decides, which is a green that lies; a command presented as read-only that wrote; and a probe that exercised a destructive operation to check it was blocked, on a table where its statement could land, which is a probe that is only harmless when it fails. What makes them two and not eleven is that the same question can be asked of all of them: what is the denominator of this figure, and what does this instrument report when it could not look. CQ-19 is about what an instrument REPORTS and hangs from step 9, which is where the full CQ catalogue already hangs; CQ-20 is about the PRIVILEGE a verification runs with and hangs from step 14, fail-closed, the pair of the red routine of step 8 -- the red first demands that a test CAN detect, and this one demands that on detecting it DOES NOT BREAK. What comes in: CQ-19 with four faces (the denominator, independence, the universe in both directions, the lax sibling) and CQ-20 with two (the undeclared effect, the probe that is only harmless when it fails), both blocking, both with their statement extracted from Annex H like every other rule and never transcribed here; the faces policy, in one single copy, declaring what a face is, that its id is append-only, that the switch-off record of project_config takes the id of a face in its `rule` field, that a rule with ANY face switched off is NEVER reported as fulfilled -- three of four faces, one switched off with its reason, never a percentage alone -- and that the count of faces is derived and never written next to the name of the collection; the count of faces in `counts`, derived; the verification question of each rule in its step; and the validator walking faces in both directions, in both languages, demanding provenance of each one, because a face is an entry that carries a requirement and a differential that does not count it leaves a project upgrading blind (D-068, D-076). Why ONE rule with faces and not six sister rules, since the six measured failures each proposed their own: the six would land on the working agreement, which is the one piece the method protects against inflation -- its own alarm says nobody respects twenty rules, six or eight get respected -- and a reader who receives six separate rules recognises the one that looks like his case and not the other five. A rule with a name leaves the QUESTION, which is what generalises to the seventh path nobody has measured yet. And the price of the shape, said plainly because it is the reason the policy above exists: a switched-off face is less visible than a switched-off rule, so the record has to be able to address one. What this version does NOT do: change any requirement, any id, any threshold or any severity of the forty-six that were already there, and it does not give CQ-18 the identifiers its five checks still lack -- that is adding and not renaming, so it can be done, and it is separate work (D-078, PND-065 to PND-068).

Two decisions enter together, because both came out of the same control and both change what a report has to CARRY rather than what a system has to be. Where they came from: the audit of step 13 of arm C1 of the A/B experiment of the method, on 2026-11-02. FIRST, the choice of the auditor gains a floor and an order (D-079). The method already preferred a model other than the one that built, citing a 2026 study, and said it was not a hard gate because sometimes the builder's model is the only one available. What it did not say is what to do when the other model IS available and is not up to the task, which is the case that got measured: the auditor on another model delivered four of the nine findings it had itself announced, its only P0 was false because it read a float of 5.666 ms as 5666 ms, and what chose it was a 306-second timeout and not a judgement about capacity. So the preference now carries its order -- another model if it is up to the task; another session of the same model, with the deviation declared, if it is not; and never an auditor chosen by which key happens to be loaded or which timeout it survives -- and the report declares which case applies under the fixed key auditor_choice, with one of its declared values. The value tool_constraint is the one that did not exist and the one that costs: a constraint of the tool disguises itself as a technical choice, and the only thing that strips it bare is having to name it. The same experiment is the reason the floor is stated and not merely suspected, and it is one datum and not a law: the auditor on the SAME model, departing from the preference and declaring it in its first line, delivered seventeen findings and none of them turned out false when the owner verified them one by one. SECOND, what a control owes when it closes (D-080). That same audit found three different ways for evidence to be in the register and not work as evidence -- a commit of 130 files and 5,886 lines with no receipt of any kind; pending items closed as shipped without their receipts, in a project that claimed in writing that the register rejects those closures; archived mutations that cannot be applied again because they lack a trailing newline -- and it found them BY CHANCE, because the auditor chose to reproduce receipts, which the prompt asks for two or three of. The method demanded evidence in several steps and nowhere demanded auditing the instrument that keeps it, so each of those three reads as a full register. Step 13 now carries the health of the register of the evidence as a dimension that is not optional, with figures a program answers -- functional commits with no receipt; closures without their receipts, and how many of those have the reason written; archived mutations that can be applied again -- and a figure that could not be measured is declared as not measured and never as zero, which is CQ-19.1. It is not optional because it is the only dimension that audits all the others: if the register of the evidence is broken, every other finding of the report rests on data nobody can reproduce. And the controls that produce findings -- step 12 honest verification, step 13 the audit, step 23 the retrospective -- now close with every finding assigned to a destination under the fixed key findings_by_destination: product if the defect is in the audited system, method if it is in the method being followed, tool if it is in the tool that runs it. Why a destination and not a free-form note: without it, whether the method improves itself depends on somebody remembering to separate the findings of the method from those of the product, and remembering is not a mechanism; and a defect of the method filed in the product's register is a defect nobody is ever going to fix, because the owner of the product cannot fix the method and whoever could never heard about it. What comes in: artifact entries and verification questions over steps 12, 13 and 23, every one of them new, every one with its since_schema and its since_version. The keys are English and ASCII and the prose around them is in the language of the project, which is D-051 and D-075 applied to a document of a project instead of to its configuration file: a key that a gate reads is a key, and auditor_choice travelling translated would be the eighty-seven names for twenty-four slots all over again. What this version does NOT do, said by its name: change any requirement, any id, any threshold or any severity of what was already there; make the gate of step 13 blocking where it only warns today -- the Auditor: line is still a should_contain, and whether the completeness of an audit can be read by a machine at all is separate work --; and give the figures of the health of the register their own threshold ids, because the method does not fix with what each one is measured and that stays with whoever measures (D-075). (D-079, D-080.)

Two decisions enter together, because both are about the same thing: a step whose work is done outside, where the gate can look at the trace and never at the work. Step 13 has its work in another session and step 10 has it in a person, and until now both read as fulfilled while the thing they are there for had not happened. FIRST, what a report declares about itself (D-081). Measured on 2026-11-02: an audit report that said of itself, literally, that it had found nine findings, was writing four and was incomplete came out green, because being complete is not a property of a file -- it is the relation between what a report announces and what it delivers -- and a gate that looks at the file cannot see it. A bigger budget does not fix it either: that session was not cut off, it ended by itself in one turn and emitted its closing marker on its own, so a gate cannot tell a report that ran out of room from one that was abandoned. What enters is therefore about the trace and not the work: the report declares its completeness under audit_completeness, with findings_announced and findings_written carrying their figures, which is what makes the claim falsifiable by anybody willing to count; the grade of each audited dimension under dimension_grades, which the prompt already asked for and nothing verified; the verdict of each reproduced receipt under receipts_reproduced, because a receipt that was only read has no verdict; and what was not audited under not_audited, where nothing left out travels without its pending item. None of them prevents a lie. All of them turn the lie into a written claim with a date on it instead of a silence. And the method now says in its own prose what none of this changes: step 13 cannot be verified end to end by a machine, and saying so is worth more than simulating it. SECOND, the walk and the debt (D-082). Step 10 asks for manual cases to be written and forbids the agent to mark them as executed, because execution is human; so in a project where nobody executes, the step advanced with its artifact complete and its purpose unmet, and a compliance document claimed six criteria as verified whose verifier was a person who never ran them. The method cannot compel a person, and a gate that demanded one could only be satisfied by lying. So what the step demands is the declaration, which an agent can make honestly: cases_written, cases_executed_by_a_person -- moved only by a signed execution and never by the reading of the agent -- and execution_debt, naming who owes which execution and since when. What enters is the DECLARATION and not a new blocking condition: the figure is not required to be above zero. And that is said with its measurement, because the first wording of this entry claimed the debt does not stop the step and that is false for a project on the catalogue of today -- step 10 has declared manual_cases_per_profile as required since 2026.10.1, which is anchor 4 of Annex H, and an installation that implements it goes red when nobody signed a single case, measured with the real evaluator on 2026-11-02. The project where the step advanced with an empty execution table was running the frozen schema 1, where the only check of step 10 is that the file exists. So what was missing was never a block: it was that the debt be legible, with its figure and the name of whoever owes it, instead of an empty register saying nobody signed without saying who had to sign. And the other half is a requirement the method did not have: the agentic walk through the screens, distinct from the human execution and never a replacement for it -- the agent walks to find defects, a person executes to accept. It was measured to be what found the most interface defects in a full cycle, and the method was not asking for it; the agent was asking it of itself. It goes to a file of its own with its denominator: how many screens the system has, how many were walked, how many defects came out, and a screen that could not be reached counted inside the total with its reason, which is CQ-19.1. What comes in: artifact entries and verification questions over steps 10 and 13, every one of them new, every one with its since_schema and its since_version, and one new artifact path, which the contract of its step names in the eight languages. The keys are English and ASCII and the prose around them is in the language of the project (D-051, D-075). What this version does NOT do, said by its name: change any requirement, any id, any threshold or any severity of what was already there; add an evaluator that compares the two figures of the completeness arithmetically, because an evaluator that an installation does not know stops the step for every consumer, and two figures written by the same hand do not check each other -- the comparison against the body of the report is the owner's verification and it is published as such; make the human execution of the manual cases a condition to advance, which is the thing the method cannot produce; and declare who verifies each criterion of the usability document, which is separate work. (D-081, D-082.)

Two decisions enter together, and both are the same question asked of a step whose verdict depends on a person: what does the method say when nobody signed, and who says that a criterion is met. FIRST, the answer step 10 owed (D-083). The prose that entered with D-082 said, correctly, that the declaration of the debt does not add a gate of its own, and left a reader able to conclude the opposite of what the gate does: that step 10 advances with nobody having executed anything. Measured on 2026-11-02 with the real evaluator, both halves are of one piece: with the register of signatures empty the step comes out red saying that nobody signed a single case, and with ONE case signed by a person -- with their name, their date and the profile they ran it with -- that same tree, with its thirteen written cases and its execution_debt at pending_verifier, stops being red and goes to the owner's verification. So what stops the step is not the debt and never was: it is that nobody signed anything, and that has been in anchor 4 of Annex H since 2026.10.1. What comes in is a verification question of the owner, and nothing else: the requirement was already there, what was missing was that the text of the step answer the same thing the gate answers, and that is prose and lives in the contract, in the eight languages. The owner asked, when the lot was commissioned, that the human execution not be a condition to advance; what the measurement says is that it already was one, by a published requirement that pinned projects carry, so relaxing it would be editing a requirement and that goes with its own decision. This one does not relax it: it makes it legible. SECOND, who verified each criterion (D-084). The method demanded, since anchor 3, that the compliance documents report result by result, and nowhere demanded that they say WHO said so, so a criterion a program verifies and a criterion a person judges read the same. It was measured: a compliance document had to be corrected on 2026-11-02 and six criteria went from verified to not verifiable, one single one staying verified, because the verifier of the others was a person who never executed the cases. The agent had not lied; the document had nowhere to say whose the criterion was. What comes in, over docs/CODE_QUALITY.md and docs/USABILITY.md: the declaration with its denominator -- criteria_total counting the rules nobody verified yet, which is CQ-19.1 asked of a compliance document, criteria_verified_by_a_program, criteria_verified_by_a_person signed with a name and a date, and verification_debt with its pending verifier -- and, criterion by criterion, verified_by with the instrument the catalogue ALREADY declares for that rule, which is why the verifier is derived and not chosen: the data has said since it exists that a manual_case is judged by a person and returns passed or failed with a name and a date. The two documents and not only the one the finding named, because the data says four code-quality rules are judged by a manual case too, and fixing one half would reproduce the defect in the other. The keys are English and ASCII and the prose around them is in the language of the project (D-051, D-075). What this version does NOT do, said by its name: change any requirement, any id, any threshold or any severity of what was already there; relax anchor 4, which is what a project pinned to a published version carries and what the owner decides in its own entry; add an evaluator that compares the figures of the compliance document arithmetically, for the same reason D-081 did not add one -- the vocabulary of evaluators is append-only and a name an installation does not know stops the step for every consumer, and three figures written by the same hand do not check each other, so the comparison is the owner's verification and is published as such; and give those figures their own threshold ids, because the method does not fix with what each one is measured (D-075). (D-083, D-084.)

One rule enters, with three faces, and the three faces are the three defects of the second batch of the same A/B experiment: a correct artefact that never reaches the one place where it has an effect (D-087). What makes them one rule and not three is that the same question can be asked of all of them -- how far did this run reach, and which part of the artefact was left uncrossed -- which is the form D-078 used for the eleven failures of the first batch. FIRST, the port with a double (CQ-21.1). One arm built its view on a port with its test double, which is what the method pushes you to do so that the view is verifiable, and the port listened for a single kind of event while four of the five controls emitted another: four dead controls in a browser with eighty-one test files green on top, one of which asserted exactly what was broken, green because it walked the listeners of the fake node and called them by hand. The wording is not the method's: the first one asked for a test that crosses it for real against the real implementation, and the arm refuted it with its own code -- one of its tests already ran the real adapter against a fake document that invoked the listener without looking at the event, so it crossed the real implementation and still never saw the defect. What stays is that the other side has to be the REAL other side, whatever the port is doubling: a browser, an operating system, a database, the network. Its cost was measured by the arm, which is the objection the face will get: one run, 15.6 seconds, zero new packages. SECOND, written is not run (CQ-21.2). A closing that touches manual cases declares its reach in the honest report -- cases_touched, cases_with_an_execution_row and executed_by -- and not only in the file where the case lives: the figures of the file entered with D-082 and they are in the right place, but a figure somebody has to go and look for stops nobody, and the report is what the owner reads every time. THIRD, the case comes back whole (CQ-21.3). A case with two demands in one step failed on the first, the absence was fixed, the correction closed on the verification of the step that failed, and the second demand was never verified: the button appeared and did nothing, because it was one of the four dead controls. An execution row reports how far the person got; the steps it did not reach neither passed nor failed, and closing on that row confuses not having seen it fail with having seen it work. So a case that failed and was fixed comes back whole and leaves a row later than the fix, under the fixed key rerun_after_a_fix. What comes in: one rule with its three faces, every one of them new and with its since_schema and its since_version; artifact entries and verification questions over steps 8, 10, 11 and 12; one new family in the producer-consumer map of step 11 -- the ports that were doubled for testing, with ports_total, ports_with_a_crossing_run and, per port, its adapter, its double and the crossing run naming what is on the other side -- so that a port with no crossing run is a declared hole instead of an absence nobody wrote down. The keys are English and ASCII and the prose around them is in the language of the project (D-051, D-075). What this version does NOT do, said by its name: change any requirement, any id, any threshold or any severity of what was already there; add an evaluator, for the reason D-081 and D-084 already recorded -- the vocabulary is append-only and a name an installation does not know stops the step for every consumer; promise that a gate can verify that the declared run crosses the port for real, which it cannot and which is written in the annex and in the contract instead of being simulated; and give these figures their own threshold ids, because the method does not fix with what each one is measured (D-075). (D-087.)

Three rules come in and one published rule gains a face, from the third batch of findings of the A/B experiment of the method: ten findings, nine of them left by arm C1 on closing the twenty-four steps -- twenty-two of twenty-four with no override -- and one from an analysis of tooling platforms. The line that unifies almost all of them belongs to the owner: do not accept "the measurement exists" as a criterion. CQ-22 (Contrast, BLOCKS, four faces, anchored at steps 14, 19 and 20) asks what a figure is contrasted against and who decided: step 19 of the arm closed GREEN with its non-functional requirement unmet -- p95 from 557 to 911 ms against a declared ceiling of 300, at two hundred concurrent users -- and the gate that let it through is right about what it measures, because it verifies that the receipt exists and carries its thresholds or the written impossibility. Its four faces are four halves of the same hole: the figure against its threshold, the threshold with its condition (the requirement said p95 < 300 ms and did not say at what concurrency, so the same system passes at twenty people and fails at two hundred), the declared absence that does not close a step (step 20 closed green over a recovery manual whose section 6 says, verbatim, that there are no backups of anything), and every entry of an inventory with its decision, which is the caveat the tenth finding brought written. CQ-23 (Provenance, BLOCKS, three faces, anchored at steps 8, 9 and 12) asks whether a verdict is about this work and whether it still exists: a green that is true and old because the chain ran before the change that broke it and the hook that looks at the definitive tree only runs on publishing; a run whose output travelled inside the response and was lost whole, against the same chain whose output landed on disk and survived; and a step green and not done, whose two checks were satisfied by the same two files of the previous step. The wording of CQ-23.3 is the arm, not the method, and it is credited as such: which file of this list did not exist before starting? CQ-24 (Register, BLOCKS, two faces, anchored at steps 5, 11 and 23) asks whether a register can answer the question it exists for over the whole of its stretch: zero items of a hundred and ninety-five with the forced-close field written against twenty-eight that name it in prose and ten closes the prose declares forced, in the only project that ever reached the retrospective the field exists for; plus a second independent occurrence in another system, where an append-only record carried a constant motive field, true of the first row and false of the three that followed. Two independent occurrences make it a family, so the face is worded for the family -- a mandatory field whose value is not derived from the fact it says it records -- and not for the field that brought it in. The second face is the register born halfway: twelve anti-patterns entering in one commit at step 11, with steps 00 to 04 reporting zero incidents, which is not the absence of incidents but the absence of a register. And CQ-21 gains CQ-21.4, which is the first time a published rule gains a face after entering: a mutation declared caught because the test went red, when it went red on a type error and never reached the assertion. It comes in as a face and not as a rule because the question that detects it is the question of CQ-21 word for word -- how far did the run get -- and the statement of the rule already says that a step no execution reached neither passed nor failed. Faces go from nine to nineteen and the count of rules from forty-nine to fifty-two (24 of code quality and 28 of usability). Coming in with them, as requirements of their steps: the restore drill of step 20 (docs/RESTORE_DRILL.md, a run that destroyed and restored with the rows counted before and after and the schema at its migration) with the new threshold acceptable_data_loss_window, which the OWNER declares and neither the method nor the agent assumes; the inventory of the third-party code the system EXECUTES at step 14 (docs/THIRD_PARTY_EXECUTION.md) with the privilege of each entry and a decision per entry; the thresholds of step 19 with their denominator, their verdict and the condition of each one; and the proof at step 22 that from ONE real error the system can say what it was, because a counter of 5xx counts without being able to look at what it counts. No id was recycled, no existing requirement was edited and no severity moved. What this version does NOT do, said by its name: verify that the figure a project declares is the one it measured. What a machine looks at is the declaration -- the verdict next to the figure, the condition next to the threshold, the decision of each entry, the date of a verdict against that of the last change -- and the truth of the declaration is decided by a person reading, which is the same border CQ-21 wrote into its own section (D-089, PND-105 to PND-116).

languages.note: The prose of the method (docs/) is written in Spanish, which is the source of truth, and published in every language listed in `prose_versions`. The data layer (gates/ and the published file) is written in English, which is the canonical language of the profession, because it is not part of the translated corpus. Translating for the comprehension of an end user is the job of the consumer tool, not of this catalogue.
languages.exception: The frozen base (gates/baseline.json) keeps the Spanish text and the `tramo` field name it had when the method took ownership. The base is not edited: changing it is a change of the method, with its own decision.

text_language.what: Which language each human-readable text of this file is in. It is declared mechanically because the file is bilingual: reading `data` as a single language would make a consumer show Spanish to an English reader.
text_language.rule: Inside the keys listed in `spanish_scope`, a text is Spanish when neither its own node nor any enclosing node declares `since_schema` >= 2: it comes from the frozen base, and the base is not edited. A node with `since_schema` >= 2 is new, and its text is English. Every text outside `spanish_scope` is English.
text_language.language_neutral: Ids, step and station keys, evaluator names, enum values, file paths and the regular expressions of must_contain / should_contain are not prose and carry no language. The regular expressions are deliberately bilingual, so that a gate matches a document written in either language.
text_language.verified: The method checks this declaration on every build: every text the rule calls Spanish has to appear literally in gates/baseline.json, and no text the rule calls English may read as Spanish. If the declaration stops being true, nothing is published.
text_language.consumer: Do not print these texts to an end user. Read the stable `id` -- an opaque key that is never translated -- and take the text from your own catalogue. That holds for the English texts too: this file is the definition of the gates, not a translated user interface.

languages.prose_versions_what: The languages the prose of the method is published in, declared as a LIST and not as a count inside a sentence. The method declares ITS OWN languages: if they coincide with those of some other specification, that is a coincidence and not a definition. Adding a language changes this array and no prose anywhere, which is why the array exists -- the claim used to live in a sentence here, in the prompt corpus, in two README files and in forty strings of the landing page, and correcting one of them meant mechanically raising two declared versions.
